# Runtime vendor provenance

## Three.js 0.187.0 — locally minified derivatives

`three.module.js` and `three.core.js` are minified from the exact Three.js 0.187.0 package, runtime revision 187. They retain their original relative import URLs and public exports. `THREE-LICENSE.txt` and the MIT license header in each module are retained.

Source: <https://registry.npmjs.org/three/-/three-0.187.0.tgz>. Preserved archive SHA-256: `ff540832ded0cfe919764d24a3d88f3e2a05f23303f876423e4f893841e90728`.

| Module | Original bytes | Generated bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `three.module.js` | 658,900 | 374,603 |
| `three.core.js` | 1,474,799 | 395,577 |
| Total | 2,133,699 | 770,180 |

This removes 1,363,519 bytes (63.9%) before HTTP compression. It is a file-size measurement, not a measured improvement to page-load time. No unused-feature removal or geometry changes were made. The preserved downloaded source is unchanged.

### Rebuilding

From the project directory, supply an extracted Three.js package root and the exact minifier bundle explicitly:

```sh
node website/prepare-vendor.mjs \
  --source-dir /path/to/three-0.187.0 \
  --terser /path/to/pinned-terser/bundle.min.js
```

`--output-dir /path/to/vendor-directory` is optional; the default is `website/public/assets/vendor` (the source copied into `site/assets/vendor` by the website build). The script checks the package name/version, both source file hashes, license hash, minifier bundle hash and expected generated hashes before writing. It rejects unexpected edits in existing output modules or the license. It does not download or install anything. Generated modules can be used directly without rebuilding or including build tools in the website.

Tool: Terser 5.27.0 as declared by its Next.js 16.1.7 host. The vendored Terser package has no embedded version; therefore the script requires this exact bundle SHA-256: `e4ae9a64825ea7f53606c3ee01633f08b64e12000a30d3687f52b64977f9a652`. An arbitrary Terser 5.27.0 distribution is not asserted to have the same bundle bytes. Terser is BSD-2-Clause licensed and is not shipped as a runtime asset. A fresh checkout needs either the already generated files or a separately supplied matching build tool and source package.

Options and all input/output hashes are recorded in `three-build-provenance.json`. Output is UTF-8 with no appended newline, preserving the expected generated hashes.

## Scroll Craft — one documented local runtime patch

Source repository: [nateherkai/scroll-craft](https://github.com/nateherkai/scroll-craft/tree/75d81f74e83692add18cd7a8a8e078b8a887a579), commit `75d81f74e83692add18cd7a8a8e078b8a887a579`.

Original file: `plugins/nateherk-design/skills/scroll-craft/engine/scrollcraft.js`.

- Upstream source: 62,176 bytes; SHA-256 `4a419b3ede51f64790af7b56c0195ea01c98a84df8e0e768ebf343956b922f39`.
- Locally patched runtime: 62,282 bytes; SHA-256 `c6488f0ae011e95accfc46a91eb4f46933fcae4d909257e4c550ba25cd886058`.
- MIT license is preserved in `SCROLLCRAFT-LICENSE.txt`; SHA-256 `dd471a27eca72488a53e6ea6fbe9392d81aa3f01e950e63fe328affb2ddfa6e3`.

The only runtime change is at startup, immediately after `layout(); initPointer();`:

```diff
-    scTickFrame = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
+    // Local patch: all clips are collected; pages without video need no seek loop.
+    if (playheads.length) scTickFrame = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
```

The upstream startup begins a video-seeking loop even when no video clips exist. The local condition avoids that recurring work. Clip collection is synchronous before this point; no dynamic clip-registration API exists. The loop body, scroll event handling, pointer effects and cleanup remain unchanged. This is a local source modification, not an upstream configuration option. The downloaded reference and shared stylesheet remain unchanged.
